evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from quantitative data showing that combined binding capacity produces greater apical enrichment than either binding site alone.

claim: Apical recruitment of Dia is mediated by binding to two distinct elements, PI(4,5)P2 and Rho1.
source_text: We found that apical recruitment of Dia is mediated by binding to two distinct elements, PI(4,5)P2 and Rho1.
evidence_reasoning: This claim summarizes the experimental findings demonstrating the roles of both PI(4,5)P2 and Rho1 in Dia localization.

claim: Synergism between PI(4,5)P2 and Rho1 ensures highly efficient apical localization of active Dia.
source_text: Further analysis suggests that synergism between these two partial signals ensures highly efficient apical localization of active Dia.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from quantitative data showing enhanced apical enrichment when both binding domains are intact.

claim: Binding to Rho1 alone was weak but nevertheless detectable.
source_text: Binding to Rho1 alone was weak but nevertheless detectable.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by data showing that the ΔBD construct (which can bind Rho1 but not PI(4,5)P2) shows some apical enrichment.

claim: Binding to PI(4,5)P2 alone was not capable of generating any apical localization bias.
source_text: Conversely, binding to PI(4,5)P2 alone was not capable of generating any apical localization bias, despite its marked contribution to apical recruitment in the presence of Rho1
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by data showing that the BD alone does not drive apical localization.

claim: Binding to activated Rho1 may represent the more prevalent scenario for the initial interaction of Dia with the apical membrane.
source_text: Binding to activated Rho1 may represent the more prevalent scenario for the initial interaction of Dia with the apical membrane.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is speculative, inferred from the observation that Rho1 binding alone can provide some apical bias while PI(4,5)P2 binding alone cannot.

claim: Rho1 binding gives rise to an open conformation of Dia, which is more amenable to targeting.
source_text: This interaction will also give rise to an open conformation of Dia, which is more amenable to targeting, and will provide physical proximity to the membrane.
evidence_reasoning: This claim combines established knowledge about Rho1-mediated Dia activation with data showing enhanced apical localization of the open form.

claim: Membrane proximity allows the interaction of Dia with PI(4,5)P2, which was not favored when the Dia protein was cytoplasmic, due to low affinity restrictions.
source_text: Membrane proximity can now allow the interaction of Dia with PI(4,5)P2, which was not favored when the Dia protein was cytoplasmic, due to low affinity restrictions.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the observation that PI(4,5)P2 binding requires Rho1 binding, suggesting that membrane proximity facilitates the weak PI(4,5)P2 interaction.

claim: The Dia-PI(4,5)P2 interaction stabilizes association with the apical membrane.
source_text: The Dia-PI(4,5)P2 interaction stabilizes association with the apical membrane, resulting in synergy in the combined action of Rho1 and PI(4,5)P2 in Dia apical localization.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the synergistic effects observed when both binding domains are intact.

claim: Once in the vicinity of the apical membrane, Dia can shift dynamically among three states: being bound to each of the cues alone, or to both simultaneously.
source_text: Once in the vicinity of the apical membrane, Dia can shift dynamically among three states, being bound to each of the cues alone, or to both simultaneously.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is speculative, proposing a dynamic model based on the observation that both cues contribute to localization.

claim: The activity of N-WASP is dependent on the synergistic binding of the Rho GTPase Cdc42 and of PI(4,5)P2 to distinct domains in the protein.
source_text: The activity of N-WASP, the activator of the ARP2/3 actin nucleation complex, was shown to be dependent on the synergistic binding of the Rho GTPase Cdc42 and of PI(4,5)P2 to distinct domains in the protein.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Prehoda et al., 2000 and Padrick and Rosen, 2010.

claim: Synergistic binding of Cdc42 and PI(4,5)P2 to N-WASP does not lead to targeting of the protein to distinct subcellular domains, but rather to localized activation.
source_text: However, this binding is not reported to lead to targeting of the protein to distinct subcellular domains, but rather to localized activation
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the cited literature about N-WASP regulation.

claim: dia mRNA is apically localized by a mechanism that is distinct from the protein localization machinery.
source_text: As previously noted, dia mRNA is also apically localized by a mechanism that is distinct from the protein localization machinery, leading to localized translation of Dia protein at the apical membrane
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Massarwa et al., 2009).

claim: Endogenous Dia displays a more restricted apical distribution compared with over-expressed protein.
source_text: Indeed, we observed a more restricted apical distribution of endogenous Dia compared with the over-expressed protein, which is not localized at the RNA level
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by comparison of endogenous Dia staining (Figure 1A-C) with expressed GFP-Dia constructs.

claim: This general mechanism in Drosophila tubular organs likely extends to tubular tissues in the mammalian system.
source_text: It is likely that this general mechanism in Drosophila tubular organs extends to tubular tissues in the mammalian system.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is speculative, based on conservation of the mechanism and supporting evidence from mammalian systems.

claim: A collaboration between PI(4,5)P2 and a Rho-family GTPase in membrane recruitment of mammalian mDia2 was observed in a cell culture system.
source_text: A collaboration between PI(4,5)P2 and a Rho-family GTPase in membrane recruitment of mammalian mDia2 was observed in a cell culture system
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Gorelik et al., 2011.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 influences Dia targeting in mammalian MDCK cysts.
source_text: and here we have demonstrated the capacity of PI(4,5)P2 to influence Dia targeting in mammalian MDCK cysts
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing PI(4,5)P2-dependent relocalization of Dia in MDCK cysts.

claim: Activated mDia1 is targeted to the apical membrane in the tubular epithelium of secretory acinar cells in the mouse pancreas.
source_text: In this context, we have recently examined the tubular epithelium of secretory acinar cells in the mouse pancreas, and shown that activated mDia1 is targeted to the apical membrane
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Geron et al., 2013.

claim: The Dia apical-targeting machinery appears to be common to a variety of tubular tissues, regardless of their origin or physiological function.
source_text: Thus, the Dia apical-targeting machinery appears to be common to a variety of tubular tissues, regardless of their origin or physiological function.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from observations across multiple tubular tissues in Drosophila and evidence from mammalian systems.
